harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent sudo command auditing on node1. Commands are written to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with timestamp, invoking user, target user, and command, without duplication to /var/log/messages or /var/log/secure. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remain unchanged. Restart persistence was verified.
actions_performed: Added validated sudoers settings for a dedicated log, four-digit year, unwrapped entries, and disabled syslog duplication.
Created the root-owned mode-0600 audit log and a compatible monthly logrotate policy.
Preserved the previous sudoers file at /etc/sudoers.pre-sudo-command-logging.
Restarted node1 once and verified configuration, historical audit data, new command logging, and syslog recovery.

evidence.requirement: Record sudo commands with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Sudoers parses successfully; entries include year, time, invoking user, target user, and command. The protected log remains root-owned mode 0600.

evidence.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Test commands were present in the dedicated audit log and absent from both /var/log/messages and /var/log/secure, before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software
evidence.summary: CentOS 5.11, kernel 2.6.18-398.el5, and installed sudo 1.7.2p1 were retained; no packages were installed.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 83b5159a-9612-419e-8000-000000000000; reboot was acknowledged, the node became unavailable, and returned with boot ID 7513d01a-03f1-4013-8000-000000000000. Syslog recovered, sudoers remained valid, configuration checksums matched, pre-restart audit data persisted, and a new post-restart command was logged correctly.
